Button.reason: Ember's `primary` getter is `args.primary || args.type === 'primary'`; @type still defaults to 'primary' when only @tertiary={{true}} is passed (there is no separate 'off' value), so `cds--btn--tertiary` and `cds--btn--primary` are both added instead of just `cds--btn--tertiary`. @carbon/react's `kind='tertiary'` only ever adds `cds--btn--tertiary`. Real bug, tracked as a follow-up.
Same `type` defaults to 'primary' bug as the `tertiary` variant above, for @ghost={{true}} - `cds--btn--ghost` and `cds--btn--primary` both get added. Real bug, tracked as a follow-up.

Link.reason: Verified against ember-element-helper@0.8.8's actual source (dist/helpers/element.js): `element` (used here for @as) resolves to a dynamically-generated class that extends classic `@ember/component`, and classic tag-having components always add the framework's own `ember-view` class to their root element. @carbon/react's Link has no equivalent. This is unavoidable *while the root tag is rendered through `element`* - not an inherent Link limitation: `element` is only needed to support @as, so a `{{#if @as}}` branch rendering a literal `<a>` for the common no-@as case would avoid this (and the sibling id entry below) for every variant except as-button. Left as-is here since restructuring Link is out of scope for adding this parity test; worth doing as its own follow-up. The same artifact will hit Grid/GridColumn/GridRow when that family is added to this harness, since they also render their root tag via `element`. Applies to every variant, including as-button (button.classes[ember-view]).

Same ember-element-helper artifact as the ember-view class above - a classic tag-having component also gets an auto-generated `elementId` (rendered as the `id` attribute) by default, canonicalized here to `#1` since it's not referenced by anything else in the tree. Applies to every variant, including as-button (button.attributes.id).
Same ember-view artifact as the `a.classes[ember-view]` entry above, for the as-button variant's <button> root.
Same auto-generated-id artifact as the `a.attributes.id` entry above, for the as-button variant's <button> root.

Tag.reason: @carbon/react's Tag spreads `disabled` straight onto its root element regardless of tag type, so a non-interactive (div-rendered) disabled Tag still carries a `disabled="true"` attribute alongside the `cds--tag--disabled` class. Ember's Tag only ever adds the class, never the attribute. Real gap, tracked as a follow-up.

Loading.reason: Ember's inline branch hardcodes `style='margin-left: 1rem; width: initial; display: inline-flex; align-items: center;'` on the root div; @carbon/react's InlineLoading sets no inline style at all (its layout comes entirely from `cds--inline-loading`'s own CSS). Real gap, tracked as a follow-up.
Same hardcoded inline-style gap as `margin-left` above.
Same hardcoded inline-style gap as `margin-left` above.
Same hardcoded inline-style gap as `margin-left` above.

@carbon/react's InlineLoading renders its inner spinner via `Loading`, which sets `aria-atomic='true'` on that div; Ember's inline branch never sets `aria-atomic` at all (only its non-inline `withOverlay`/plain branches do). Real gap, tracked as a follow-up.

Ember's inline branch hardcodes a literal `aria-label='Active loading indicator'` on the spinner div (not bound to `@description`); @carbon/react's InlineLoading never puts a label on the wrapping div at all, only on the svg. Real gap, tracked as a follow-up.

@carbon/react's InlineLoading passes its own `iconDescription` (defaulting to the literal string "loading", NOT `description`) to the inner spinner's aria-label/title - `description` only ever reaches the separate visible text below. Ember's inline branch has no separate `iconDescription` concept and reuses `@description` for both, so the icon's label differs from React's default whenever a caller passes a real @description. Real gap, tracked as a follow-up.

Loading.path: div > div[0] > div[0] > svg[0] > title[0] > text("loading")[0]
Loading.reason: Same `iconDescription` vs `description` gap as the svg aria-label above - the <title> text mirrors whichever value was actually used for the label.

AiChatReasoningSteps.reason: Harness limitation, not a real gap - verified by hand that Ember's `ReasoningStep` sets `role='listitem'` on its own rendered root, matching upstream's `reasoning-step.ts` `connectedCallback` (`this.setAttribute('role', 'listitem')`) exactly. `flattenComposedTree` (see dom-parity/lib/flatten-composed-tree.mjs) deliberately does not merge a custom element host's own light-DOM attributes onto its unwrapped shadow content, since doing so can't distinguish a genuine self-applied output attribute like this one from a configuration-input attribute (see that file's own doc comment) - so upstream's host-only `role` is invisible to this diff, and only Ember's copy of it shows up, as 'extra'.
Same harness limitation as the div[0].role entry above, for the second (interactive) step - only reachable in the open-with-steps variant, which renders two steps.

Real gap, but out of scope for this harness (fixing it touches every icon in the addon); worth its own follow-up.
